2026-09-11T03:25:06.6641825Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6642436Z 
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6643110Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6643939Z 
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6644540Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6645381Z 
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6648019Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6651116Z >
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6655428Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6662863Z >
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6665372Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6666736Z 
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6667024Z ### How to Use
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6667413Z 
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6668539Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6670403Z 
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6670694Z ```bash
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6671556Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6672912Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6673945Z ```
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6674281Z 
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6674685Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6676675Z ```bash
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6677552Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6678869Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6680283Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6682750Z ```
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6683090Z 
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6684100Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6685600Z ```bash
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6686585Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6689013Z ```
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6689348Z 
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6689839Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6690831Z ```bash
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6691704Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6693347Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6696024Z ```
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6696358Z 
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6696784Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6697501Z 
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6700007Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6703638Z 
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6703921Z ```bash
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6704647Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6706073Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6708734Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6709256Z 
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6709997Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6711710Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6713888Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6714681Z ```
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6715006Z 
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6716307Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6717987Z 
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6718257Z ```bash
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6720914Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6722438Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6723808Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6725623Z 
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6726295Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6727659Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6728568Z ```
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6728900Z 
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6729231Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6731193Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6733405Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6735056Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6737270Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6739783Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6740694Z 
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6740975Z ### Notes
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6741325Z 
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6742384Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6745580Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6747753Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6750481Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6752555Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6755178Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6756844Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6758045Z </mcp-clis>
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6758679Z <github-context>
2026-09-11T03:25:06.6759906Z The following GitHub context information is available for this workflow:
